title.narrative: ITP 308 SGU Mine Water and Mine Waste Management
ITP 308 SGU Tillsyn av avfall och vattenföroreningar från gruvor

description.narrative:
Insatsens avsedda effekt är att höja kapacitet och kunskap hos nyckelpersoner inom institutioner organisationer med mandat att reglera och påverka utsläpp till vatten från gruvdrift och mineralutvinningens föroreningar till vatten. I förlängningen antas att dessa nyckelpersoner kan påverka den institutionella kontexten och förutsättningarna för en miljömässigt, demokratiskt och socialt god styrning av gruvindustri och mineralutvinning.
The intended effect of the initiative is to increase the capacity and knowledge of key personnel within institutions and organizations with a mandate to regulate and influence water emissions from mining and mineral extraction's pollution to water. In the long run, it is assumed that these key persons can influence the institutional context and conditions for environmentally, democratically and socially sound governance of the mining industry and mineral extraction.
The programme aims to build capacity in government organisations from selected African countries. Focus areas are of technical knowledge as well as integrating more efficient and ethical governance principles into mining and mine waste management, where transparency, equality and stakeholder engagements play large roles. In addition, the ITP provides an opportunity for participants to collaborate and learn from each other to improve practices and governance within the mining sector. The long-term intended impact of ITP 308 is: • The partner organisations contribute to protection of ecosystems on land and in water and promote that good living conditions and biodiversity are ensured for current and future generations • The partner organisations contribute to sustainable mining with strong socio-economic development in a peaceful and inclusive society.
By the end of 2025, the programme is expected to have contributed to six outcomes related to the participating partner organisations: 1. Efficient and ethical governance principles within partner organisations leading to a sustainable mining sector with increased accountability. 2. Effective dissemination and knowledge transfer of sustainable mineral extraction and its contribution to local and national development. 3. Partner organisations ensure the best possible scrutiny of environmental impacts, prevention and mitigation at all stages of the mine cycle. 4. Partner organisations use transparent, inclusive, and meaningful dialogue to ensure full public participation. 5. Gender discrepancy is continuously targeted within the partner organisations. 6. Strengthened collaboration between partner organisations within and between the participating countries.

Sveriges Geologiska Undersökning (SGU) har tillsammans med Naturvårdsverket och Luleå tekniska universitet (LTU) inkommit med ett förslag till ett internationellt kapacitetsutvecklingsprogram (ITP) inriktad på att stärka kapaciteten hos kontrollmyndigheter som utför tillsyn av gruvor med speciellt fokus på avfall och det vatten som sprider föroreningar från avfallet. Kapacitetsutvecklingsrogrammet är även öppet för övriga relevanta deltagare ur civila samhället, privata sektorn och akademin.
Insatsens föreslagna budget i programförslaget är SEK 59 072 348 och ska genomföras under åren 2017- 2024. De planerade programomgångarna om 25 deltagare (maximalt 30) vardera är i dagsläget. Sida tar beslut om SEK 60 100 000 för att även möjliggöra planerings-och rekryteringsfas i samband med inkludering av nya länder. Avtalet styr vilken motprestation avtalsparten behöver göra för att nyttja denna post. Inom ramen för befintlig budget kan även SGU i dialog med Sida genomföra riktade kortkurser, exempelvis för deltagande organisationers/institutioners chefer eller särskilda training of trainers-satsningar.
Initialt fokuserar programmet på tre länder som har en viktig och växande mineralutvinning - Etiopien, Tanzania och Zambia. Förstudien innefattade även en baslinje-bedömning av Rwanda, Mocambique, Mano-regionen (Elfenbenskusten, Guinea, Liberia och Sierra Leone). Programmet riktar sig till tjänstemän på relevanta myndigheter i ovan nämnda länder, samt relevanta aktörer ur civila samhället, privata sektorn samt akademien.
Programmet avser att stödja berörda tillsynsmyndigheter i arbetet med att förbättra sin leverans av tjänster genom interna förändringsprocesser. Genom att inkludera relevanta aktörer från civila samhället, privata sektorn och akademien; i såväl deltagandet som genom föreläsningar, studiebesök etc, skapas en ökad möjlighet att adressera komplexiteten i sektorn och vikten av att binda in en bred aktörsgrupp.
Programmet är uppbyggt så att det dels ger en introduktion av övergripande principer för förvaltning, miljömål, miljölagstiftning, anti-korruption, öppen data och naturresursförsörjning; samt erbjuder den vetenskapliga och tekniska bakgrund som krävs för att deltagarna ska kunna ta fram underlag för bedömningar. En viktig förutsättning för en god förvaltning och hållbar ekonomisk utveckling är kompetenta och kunniga offentliga organisationer/institutioner som agerar med integritet och som kan upprätthålla rättssäkerhet. Deltagarna får under programmets gång vägledning i genomförandet av egna förändringsprojekt förankrade i respektive hemorganisation/institution. Genom utbyten mellan deltagare från olika länder kan deltagarna också stärka sina nätverk och utbyta kunskaper och lärdomar.

The Swedish Geological Survey (SGU) has together with the Swedish Environmental Protection Agency and Luleå University of Technology (LTU) submitted a proposal for an international capacity development program (ITP) aimed at strengthening the capacity of control authorities that carry out inspections of mines with special focus on waste and the water that spreads. contaminants from the waste. The capacity development program is also open to other relevant participants from civil society, the private sector and academia. The initiative's proposed budget in the program proposal is SEK 59,072,348 and will be implemented during the years 2017-2024. The planned program rounds of 25 participants (maximum 30) each are at present. Sida decides on SEK 60,100,000 to also enable the planning and recruitment phase in connection with the inclusion of new countries. The agreement governs what consideration the contractor needs to make to use this item. Within the framework of the existing budget, SGU can also, in dialogue with Sida, conduct targeted short courses, for example for the heads of participating organizations / institutions or special training of trainers initiatives.
Initially, the program focuses on three countries that have important and growing mineral extraction - Ethiopia, Tanzania and Zambia. The feasibility study also included a baseline assessment of Rwanda, Mozambique, the Mano region (Côte d'Ivoire, Guinea, Liberia and Sierra Leone). The program is aimed at officials of relevant authorities in the above-mentioned countries, as well as relevant actors from civil society, the private sector and academia.
The program intends to support relevant regulatory authorities in the work of improving their service delivery through internal change processes. By including relevant actors from civil society, the private sector and academia; in both participation and through lectures, study visits, etc., an increased opportunity is created to address the complexity of the sector and the importance of binding a broad group of actors.
The program is structured so that it provides an introduction to overall principles for management, environmental goals, environmental legislation, anti-corruption, open data and natural resource supply; and offers the scientific and technical background required for the participants to be able to produce a basis for assessments. An important prerequisite for good governance and sustainable economic development is competent and knowledgeable public organizations / institutions that act with integrity and that can maintain legal certainty. During the program, the participants receive guidance in the implementation of their own change projects anchored in each home organization / institution. Through exchanges between participants from different countries, participants can also strengthen their networks and exchange knowledge and lessons learned.

During 2023, contributions to the ITP outcomes are catalyzed through the participants change projects which represent numerous stages in the mine cycle. The change projects vary from design and management of Tailings Storage Facilities (Zambia, Liberia, Rwanda) to training of how to practice mining responsibly at small scale or artisanal level (Tanzania), and on to the final stage of mining, i.e.mine closure (Kenya). All projects have opportunities to give positive long-term effects on the mining sector. Increased competence to better monitor and apply existing laws/regulations on environmental safety around the mining sites and safe closure of mines have been a result. Participants from Kenya, Tanz and Zambia have worked to develop guidelines for mining waste storage. They are in different stages but some have come a long way and presented to national groups responsible for the country's mining industry.
Improving the knowledge base within the government sector to reduce the knowledge gap between private and public organisations, adding further to the opportunities for enhanced governance of the mining sector has been achieved. By bringing participants who previously have not visited mine sites to the field helped increased understanding of mining governance. Building individual capacity, the partner organisations got support to ensure the best possible scrutiny of environmental impacts, prevention, and mitigation at all stages of the mine cycle.
There are several examples where the programme has contributed to improved relationships between government agencies and end users within the mining sector. One example is the Tanzanian change project Training programme for mine water and tailings management for small and medium scale mines in Tanzania. The project provided an opportunity for organisations to use transparent, and inclusive training, which according to Mining Commission officials has contributed to improved collaboration with e.g. Artisanal and Small Scale (ASM) communities. Rwanda is in the forefront of tracking and tracing minerals but have an opportunity to learn from the other participating countries about tailings management. Zambia is in the final stages of creating a Mining Commission which has been in place in Tanzania since 2017, and influences have been shared by the two countries partly a result of their ITP participation. Ethiopia (participants in groups 1-3) has been a country in the forefront on how to formalise the ASM sector and other participating countries such as Zambia, Liberia and Kenya can draw on that in their attempt for a more sustainable socioeconomic ASM sector. Liberian and Kenyan officials have looked at the Swedish Environmental Court system in mining processes as a possible way to improve their governance of the mining sector in a more transparent and efficient way for the benefit of the environment and all living organisms.
Learning about processes and legislation in the mining sector from government officials from other countries has also added to efficient and ethical governance principles, which contributes to sustainable mining. In 2023, group 6 participants answered that 93% of them had had interactions with organisations outside their country due to the ITP 308, and 100% of those, answered that their interactions had assisted in advancing the mine water and mine waste management in their organisation or country.
Key results achieved in 2023 per country as follows:
Kenya A governments key priority area for mine water and mine waste management is to have training for all artisanal miners using crude equipment and organise them into cooperatives and societies. The aim is to produce and disseminate manuals, codes or guidelines relating to environmental management and prevention or abatement of environmental degradation following from artisanal small-scale mining (ASM). As a result a positive development has seen as contribution of ITP 308 in the country is that land degradation is steadily decreasing due to increased awareness of sustainable mining practices. In general, investors appear to be more responsible when it comes to mine closure and rehabilitation than before.
Two key partner organisations in the ITP are the National Environment Management Authority (NEMA) which ensure that environmental issues are integrated into development policies, plans, programmes, and projects to create sustainable use of natural resources and the Ministry of Mining, Blue Economy and Maritime affairs (MIBEMA) which works with promoting a sustainable extractive sector in Kenya.
Formalising the artisanal small-scale mining sector by developing new guidelines and regulations has been the focus of change projects by Kenyan participants, using the knowledge provided through the ITP 308 training. Their guidance documents are to guide and supervise inspectors of mines, and to inform and enlighten the public about the environmental effects of mining. This will increase the quality and sustainability of the mining. Two change projects (groups 4-5) have developed a training manual on sustainable mining for regional committees. This manual is also to be disseminated to the artisanal miners, for them to be more successful in their operations. The toolkit for ASM in Taita Taveta County (group 6) is well interlaced with the manual for the ASM committees. These change projects have been piloted together with the very first change project about mine closure in 2023. The outcome was favorable, and it is expected that the continuance of the first Kenyan change project is going to be gazette early in 2024.
Liberia The mining industry in Liberia has been booming since 2017, and a large portion of the population has transitioned from agriculture and fishing to ASM. The continued growth of this sector is creating several challenges for the government and the environment. Formalising ASM in Liberia is also a government priority. As part of various collaborations and programs involving mining in Liberia, a number of documents and tools concerning artisanal-small-scale mining have been created in the last couple of years. A specific guideline on ASM operations has been developed under the Environmental Governance Program (EGP). The Mercury Awareness Toolkit was developed with the support of the German Agency for International Cooperation GmbH (GIZ). The Environmental Stewardship Benchmark Toolkit was created under the ITP 308- Mine water and mine waste management. Together, the guidelines, leaflet and tool kits complement each other and will assist in improving the ASM sector.
Two organisations in Liberia have participated in the ITP 308. The Ministry of Mines and Energy is responsible for monitoring and enforcing compliance on policies regarding exploration, development and exploitation of minerals, water, and energy resources and the Environmental Protection Agency manages the environment in Liberia and to coordinate, monitor and consult with stakeholder on all activities for the protection of the environment and the sustainable use of natural resource. Their change projects have focused on ASM related with training toolkits. The original Know your activity - Class C mining leaflet from group 4 was updated by group 6 in 2023 and distributed to ASM communities and regulating local authorities. Hotline contacts for both MME and EPA were also included. Apart from the updated leaflet, an Environmental Stewardship Minimum Benchmark Training Toolkit for Artisanal and Small Scale Gold Mining in Liberia was developed. This toolkit is intended for all ASM hotspots and is shared with all relevant stakeholders. The toolkit provides training and guidance to ASM operators on smart mining, restoration techniques and education on health implications of unsustainable mining practices. The results from the change projects with the toolkit and leaflet developed in collaboration with relevant government agencies and mining communities and disseminated to the concerned parties for capacity building have contributed to raised awareness of how the miners can reduce their environmental footprint while adhering to the mining guideline on ASM operations.
The materials developed from the ITP 308 have been made use for training of various kinds. The EPA has added the ITP material on sustainable mining to their in-house training of government employees, training-of-trainers, training of environmental inspectors, training of EIA inspectors (consultants in Liberia) and University classes. These have helped build capacity within their organisation, but also with relevant stakeholders regulating and monitoring the mining sector in Liberia.
Rwanda The mining industry holds a level of controversy in Rwanda due to its borders and closeness with the DRC, Burundi and Uganda and the ongoing debate of legal/illegal trading of minerals between the countries and the ongoing informal mining industry. Hence, environment and the growing mining industry related legislations and inspection are a concern for the government.
Two organisations, Rwanda Mines, Petroleum and Gas Board (RMB) and Rwanda Environment Management Authority (REMA), have been participating partners in the ITP 308. Both organisations have mandate to regulate and enforce laws and regulations related to the mining sector in Rwanda. In 2023, the Rwanda Mines, Petroleum and Gas Board (RMB) put forward their first change project, a draft guideline for tailings management facility, in the country. The draft guidelines outline steps that need to be taken by mining operators in order to manage mining wastes and protect the people and the environment. Still being piloted, the draft guideline is a first step to improve mine waste management in the country. Future change projects will aim to connect the draft guideline with a tailings management register, which is hoped to be a data repository for all active and decommissioned Tailings Manage Facilities (TMF).
Tanzania Tanzania is a country with a growing mining sector and interest from investors to boost national economy which has substantial impacts on the environment. Awareness about mining and its impact on the environment and communities has also increased generally in recent years. A number of positive outcomes of improved mining governance have surfaced lately e.g. the increased EIA scrutiny during stakeholder engagement processes has put pressure on mining companies code of conduct, both environmentally and socially. Today, EIAs are also scrutinized more rigorously before a loan for a new project is approved, all according to mining officials.
The 4 participating organisations from Tanzania in the ITP 308 are all involved with governing and enforcing regulations within the mining sector. The Ministry of Minerals (MoM) mission is to manage minerals resources through policy and legal frameworks. The Mining Commission (MC) is a body created within the MoM and supervises and regulates all mining operations by issuing licenses and permits, conducting compliance inspections, and organising awareness trainings as well as collect revenue for the government. The National Environmental Management Council (NEMC) is the overall environmental regulator and mainly review, oversee, and monitor EIA processes as well as oversee compliance and enforcement. Occupational Safety and Health Authority (OSHA) regulate safety and health matters by ensuring safe work environments through, e.g., accident investigations and awareness trainings. They also issue compliance licenses.
In 2023 there were some significant contributions to the ITP related programme outcomes and the work the participants carried out in Tanzania. Due to the change in processing of gold by mercury to cyanide (98% of the gold is recovered like this today), there is an increase in the availability of harmful, empty cyanide containers in Tanzania. To address this issue the MC and NEMC partnered with the Government Chemist Laboratory Authority, which oversees national chemical management programmes, to create draft guidelines on how to manage and dispose of empty cyanide containers in Tanzania. With no existing laws or regulations, local communities may unknowingly use these containers for water, posing serious health risks. This change project helps minimise risks to workers, communities, and the environment. A positive development is improved collaboration with a number of ASM communities as a result of enhanced dialogue stemming from a change project Guideline for mine water and tailings management for small and medium scale mines in Tanzania undertaken by group 6 in 2023. Site visits in pilot areas were carried out with a smaller pilot session held to test the prepared Guidelines in collaboration with the District Environmental Management Officers in the Shinyanga District. There are expectations that, at least, the Mining Commission and the National Environmental Management Council will engage in the training long-term and make use of the Guideline once the Training programme has been finalised.
Zambia Zambia is a major copper producer in Africa and mining plays a significant role in the countrys economy. At the same time, Zambian mining industry governance was rated as "Weak" by the Natural Resource Governance Institute, largely due to poor revenue management and rising criticisms regarding environmental management and mining governance readiness. To address these concerns, Zambia is restructuring its mining sector oversight by establishing a new Minerals Regulation Commission. This entity will facilitate effective regulation, compliance monitoring, and enforcement activities.
The ITP 308 program is working with government officials from The Ministry of Mines and Mineral Development (MMMD) and Zambia Environmental Management Agency (ZEMA).
All change projects by Zambians, between 2019 and 2023 related to mine waste management have focused on the absence of guiding documents on how to manage mining waste and the elaboration of training manuals, guidance on how to improve EIAs and to strengthen officials role in inspection and permitting. One of the projects from 2023 aimed to get previous guidelines on management of waste to become a Memorandum of Understanding between MMMD and ZEMA. Although the guidelines were not developed completely, awareness about waste management has begun to increase, and the issue has taken on a central role within regulating authorities. The work with mine waste guidelines over the years contributes to mitigating and preventing environmental damage and is shared between groups on an organizational level and between organizations.
In 2022/2023, one group compiled a report on Zambia's ASM sector legislation and policies to explore ways to simplify and enhance its formalisation. Increasing formalisation among ASM workers can make the sector safer for both the environment and people while also generating revenue for state development. Interviews with ASM representatives were also conducted, resulting in recommendations for legislators and policymakers to guide future national ASM formalization efforts. A subsequent group is currently working on guidelines aimed at assisting ASM workers to improve their working conditions, as well as reducing negative environmental impact. The report on ASM formalisation and the subsequent guidelines for safety, health and environmental management shed light on the issues associated with illegal mining activities from all the sustainability aspects.
By end of 2023, • 180 individuals have participated in the programme • 26 change projects have been produced • 14 organisations have partaken (average two in each country) • 6 countries have participated (Ethiopia, Kenya, Liberia, Rwanda, Tanzania and Zambia) • 3 groups received training live in Sweden (2018-2019) • 5 groups received training online (2021-2023) • 2 regional conferences carried out online (2021) • 3 regional conferences carried out live in Africa (2019, 2023) • 1 regional conference carried out live in Sweden (2022).
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
